products.name: Phrase (Memsource)
products.note: Enterprise localization AI; TMS; machine translation; EU-hosted; GDPR

reading.body:
Phrase is an enterprise translation platform with machine translation and API-first architecture that connects to large language models and allows agentic workflows to orchestrate localization tasks across organizations' technology stacks.

Translation infrastructure becomes strategic as AI systems proliferate across languages and geographies. Phrase's design around agent-to-agent interaction and API-first orchestration positions it to handle the multilingual workflows that emerge when AI applications scale beyond English-speaking markets. The platform's cost controls and quality gates suggest it addresses a real constraint: ensuring that AI-driven localization remains economically viable and consistent as translation volume rises with model deployment.

The data does not cover Phrase's compute footprint, power draw, or data center dependencies. It notes EU hosting and GDPR compliance but does not quantify infrastructure scale or the power requirements of its machine translation services. The company's relationship to the broader AI stack, and whether its localization bottleneck materially affects AI scaling, remains outside this record.

profile_text.body:
Phrase, founded in 2012, describes itself as an AI-powered language intelligence platform for enterprise. Its website says the platform automates localization workflows, connects tools and engines, and scales multilingual content globally. The company presents its offering around intelligent orchestration, context and personalization, control and governance, composable and connected architecture, and expertise and ecosystem.

Phrase (Memsource) is described as an enterprise localization AI with TMS, machine translation, EU hosting, and GDPR compliance. The company's site describes AI-led localization that selects from a range of engines and LLMs or routes through a customer's own models, applying them based on content type, quality requirements, and cost. It mentions tools called Auto Adapt and Quality Estimation, and says the platform unifies translation memories, terminology, style guides, quality data, and multimodal assets. The site also describes a headless, API-first architecture, Bring Your Own capabilities, a Verified Solutions Programme, and support for MCP servers and APIs.
